title: Publish KMS rotation + troubleshooting docs; update Enterprise security/admin pages; link restricted runbooks
author: Elliot Price
release_notes: Docs: Added customer-facing KMS rotation procedure and troubleshooting guide (Hosted/Dedicated/Private). Updated Enterprise admin/security pages with KMS terminology and audit event references. Added restricted links to internal runbooks and dashboards for operators/on-call.
description: Summary: This PR publishes customer-facing documentation for KMS key rotation and KMS-related troubleshooting, updates Enterprise admin/security pages to reflect new rotation semantics and audit events, and adds links to internal runbooks/dashboards (restricted). Motivation: Customers (esp. Private) need a predictable, low-downtime rotation procedure and clear failure-mode expectations; Support and SRE need consistent public-to-internal linking so tickets can be routed with the right evidence. This PR is part of the KMS integration hardening project (ENG-4217, docs tracking ENG-4246) and incorporates learnings from SUP-18441 and recent staging game-day notes. Scope: - New docs: KMS rotation overview, Private rotation step-by-step, validation checklist, and emergency rotation guidance (customer-facing language). - New docs: Troubleshooting guide for common KMS failures (timeouts/throttling/AccessDenied/Disabled key/region mismatch), including what to collect (request IDs, key IDs/aliases, breaker/cache signals) and what is safe to retry. - Updated Enterprise pages: Security FAQ deltas, Admin/KMS configuration terminology (KEK/DEK + key version pinning), and audit logging references. - Runbook linking: Adds clearly marked 'For operators (Redwood internal)' links to Confluence runbooks/dashboards, placed behind the restricted docs section and excluded from public search indexing. Non-goals: - No changes to product behavior (handled in redwood PRs). - No publication of internal-only dashboard URLs, customer identifiers, or sensitive key policy examples beyond least-privilege guidance already approved by Security. Review notes: - Terminology is aligned with ADR-0142 (scheduled vs emergency rotation; dual-read window; backwards-compat ciphertext). - Provider sections cover AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and Azure Key Vault at a high level; Private customer responsibility boundaries are called out explicitly. - Restricted links point to the SRE degradation runbook and the KMS lifecycle audit event spec, but do not copy/paste internal schemas verbatim into public pages. Testing: - docs build + link checker in CI - local preview (mkdocs serve) - manual verification that restricted pages are not in sitemap/search index (robots meta + nav exclusions) Rollout/Comms: - After merge, we’ll announce in #field-private and #support with the new public URLs and a short 'what changed' blurb. - Sales/Solutions can share the public rotation doc with enterprise prospects; internal runbook links require Redwood SSO.
commits: docs(kms): add rotation overview + procedure skeleton
docs(kms): add troubleshooting guide + evidence checklist for support
docs(enterprise): update admin/security pages with KMS rotation semantics
docs(restricted): add operator runbook links + noindex for restricted section
chore: fix broken anchors and normalize terminology (KEK/DEK, key version pinning)
illustrative_snippet: Excerpt (public troubleshooting doc): "If you observe intermittent decrypt failures during rotation, collect: (1) the error code and provider (AWS/GCP/Azure), (2) the key identifier configured (alias/URI) and the key version pin (if present), (3) the approximate time window and region, (4) whether failures correlate with increased KMS latency/throttling, and (5) any recent IAM/key policy changes. Do not paste ciphertext or customer data into tickets." Excerpt (restricted banner): "This section is for Redwood operators only. Links require SSO and may contain internal runbooks/dashboards. Do not share externally."
review_conversation: Kira Thompson (review): The Private procedure is close, but we need a clearer prerequisite list for customer-managed KMS (IAM propagation delays + region endpoint mismatch). Also please add a short 'Backout/rollback' section that is explicitly 'safe' for operators (i.e., config revert + bounded dual-read window) without promising immediate re-encryption. Elliot Price (author): Added prerequisites (region, endpoint, IAM/key policy, propagation delay note) and a rollback section that points to ADR semantics; kept re-encryption language as 'may be required depending on artifact type' to avoid over-committing. Marcus Lin (review): Two nits: 1) Remove the sentence implying we can always 'recover' from a disabled key; we can mitigate impact but not decrypt without key access. 2) The audit events list should be referenced, not enumerated in full on public pages. Use 'available upon request' for some details and point to the enterprise admin page. Elliot Price: Updated wording on disabled keys (impact + required customer action), removed the inline event table, and replaced with a short description + link to enterprise audit logging section. Hanae Suzuki (review): For Azure, can we avoid stating 'Key Vault uses key versions in the same way'? It’s subtly different in customer mental models. Also add an example of the Key Vault URI format. Elliot Price: Adjusted Azure wording to be provider-neutral and added a URI example (without implying identical semantics). Sean Gallagher (review): The troubleshooting page should explicitly tell customers not to continuously retry on throttling; mention exponential backoff and that Redwood data plane has adaptive backoff/circuit breakers. Also add an 'When to page Redwood' section and what we’ll ask for (request IDs, timestamps, region). Elliot Price: Added throttling guidance (backoff; avoid tight loops) and an escalation/evidence section (aligned with on-call playbook). Naomi Feldman (review): Please ensure the customer-facing doc aligns with product claims: rotation is 'low-downtime' but not 'no-impact'. Also add a short note on expected behavior during scheduled rotation (dual-read window) with a simple timeline. Elliot Price: Updated phrasing to 'low-downtime / minimal disruption' and added a timeline diagram (text-based) describing staged config update + validation window.
